name: Mexica ("Aztec")
notes: The people who founded Tenochtitlan (1325 CE) and led the Triple Alliance called themselves Mexica (also Culhua-Mexica). "Aztec" (from Aztécatl, "person from Aztán," their claimed ancestral homeland) was popularized by Alexander von Humboldt (1810) and cemented as the standard term by William H. Prescott’s History of the Conquest of Mexico (1843); current specialist convention is genuinely split — Camilla Townsend’s Fifth Sun (Oxford UP, 2019) uses "Mexica" throughout its text while keeping "Aztecs" in its title, and Mexican historian Alfredo López Austin has called "Aztec" a "historical impropriety," but "Aztec" remains the dominant general-literature term and functions historically as a broader label for the wider Nahua cultural sphere linked to the Triple Alliance, not merely an error. See pty_triple_alliance for the imperial polity.
